elements.justification: An emergency requiring the movement is not observable; it is read through the conduct that shows it: the subject's hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard, "both indicators flashing together", as a disabled or imperilled vehicle shows), or the subject an emergency vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle, "vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency") showing a lit warning lamp of any colour (sig.warning_lamp, "a warning lamp lit"). ru.emergency_vehicle is "not a stand-in for a responding emergency vehicle — the class alone is not responding": the class is read only together with its lit warning lamp, and an unobserved lamp leaves the exception unknown.

Authorization by subsection 3 is the permission subsection 3 states (spans e7, e10, e12-e18): a shoulder-use permission posted by a dev.regulatory_sign, "a point regulation by catalogue code", of code shoulder_use_permitted; this span joins that permission to the duty as an exception.

"vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway". "drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle is moving, drv.motion.complete_halt ("at rest at the observation ... speed at or below a tolerance the caller sets") not holding with p.halt_speed_tolerance.

"Controlled-access highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-060, "every highway to or from which ... persons have no legal right of access except at such points only"): st.controlled_access, "a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes", whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, which lists the controlled-access lane).

A portion of the highway outside a marked traffic lane or entrance or exit lane: a st.shoulder ("the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic") or a st.median_or_divider ("physical barrier or dividing section between roadways") whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or no st.lane ("a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles") overlapped at all while the subject is on the controlled-access highway. Lanes include the entrance and exit lanes of st.controlled_access. st.lane is not a lateral position within a lane: membership is read from occupancy. The controlled-access and highway regions themselves are the highway, not a portion of it outside a lane, and are not counted as such a portion.
The person driving a vehicle of the classes listed (e12-e17): the subject vehicle, admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; which vehicles are described is read from the list.

On a paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.shoulder whose paved attribute holds while it occupies the st.controlled_access region. Lawfully placed signage allowing that vehicle to use the shoulder: a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governing that shoulder (dev.governs lists the shoulder among the regions a device governs), whose structured conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold, "the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user", the class condition included). A sign is not a road feature: the permission is the sign's, read as it is posted.

"(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480;": the named class has its own class atom, ru.emergency_vehicle, "vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency", which ru.aggregate is "not a stand-in for". DEF-NRS-484A-020 includes it by its words "a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws": the jurisdiction's designation of the class as emergency is that permission; "when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law" states when the departure from other traffic laws applies, and here the law's own condition (e18, a signed paved shoulder) states when this permission applies. Only the class is read: no responding conduct is required by the words, so none is read from the class. The words borrowed through the reference e8 from NRS 484B.210 read: "(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus,".

"(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490;": a vehicle under such a permit is one the jurisdiction designates as emergency, ru.emergency_vehicle, "vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency"; the permit itself is a legal status no scene shows, read through the emergency class the vehicle carries (an observable_reading of category status). The words borrowed through the reference e8 from NRS 484B.210 read: "(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus,".

"(c) A traffic incident management vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment", kind incident_management; it is "not a stand-in for an emergency vehicle", and none is read from it. The words borrowed through the reference e8 from NRS 484B.210 read: "(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus,".

"(d) A tow car;": the named class has its own class atom, ru.official_vehicle of kind tow, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment", which ru.aggregate is "not a stand-in for". DEF-NRS-484A-280 includes it by its words "a motor vehicle which has been altered or designed and equipped for and exclusively used in the business of towing vehicles by means of a crane, hoist, tow bar, towline or dolly": the tow kind is identified by that equipment and livery; the exclusive use in the towing business is read through them (an observable_reading of category purpose). Not an emergency vehicle. The words borrowed through the reference e8 from NRS 484B.210 read: "(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus,".

"(e) A coroner vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment", kind coroner; not an emergency vehicle. The words borrowed through the reference e8 from NRS 484B.210 read: "(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus,".

"or (f) A public transit motor bus,": the named class has its own class atom, ru.transit_bus, "bus in public transit service, identifiable by its livery or route display", which ru.aggregate is "not a stand-in for". DEF-NRS-484A-030 includes it by its words "a vehicle owned by the State, a political subdivision ... designed for carrying more than 10 passengers and used for the transportation of persons, or a vehicle, other than a taxicab, designed and used for the transportation of persons for compensation": a bus in public transit service carries persons for compensation; the taxicab exclusion is already made by the atom, a taxicab being no bus. The words borrowed through the reference e8 from NRS 484B.210 read: "(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus,".

Being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway: the listed vehicle occupies (rel.occupies) a paved st.shoulder lying on (st.on_way) the st.highway it occupies; where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder: a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governs (dev.governs) that shoulder and its conditions hold for the vehicle (prim.conditions_hold). st.on_way is not nearness: the shoulder belongs to the way by the relation. The words borrowed through the reference e8 from NRS 484B.210 read: "(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus,".

compositions.quote: (a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus,
compositions.why: The reference borrows only the list of vehicle classes NRS 484B.210(4) sets forth to name which vehicles subsection 3 permits on a signed paved shoulder; no rule of NRS 484B.210 (its passing on the right, or its exemption from it) needs to apply, hold or be complied with for this duty or its exception, and the list's words are appended in this law and carried by its own elements e12-e17.

residues.why: Introduces the list of NRS 484B.210(4) as appended; the exemption from the passing rule of NRS 484B.210(1)(c)(1) it states is that section's, not this duty's, and is not read here.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle in motion (drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) with p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold) whose footprint overlaps a controlled-access highway region (rel.occupies, st.controlled_access). Exception (emergency, e1): the duty does not apply where the subject's hazard lamps flash (sig.hazard) or the subject is an emergency vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle) showing a warning lamp lit of any colour (sig.warning_lamp).
obligation: The subject's footprint overlaps no st.median_or_divider; every st.shoulder it overlaps is an authorized shoulder; and it overlaps some st.lane or some authorized shoulder. A shoulder s is authorized (subsection 3: e2, e7, e10, e12-e18) where the subject is a listed vehicle — ru.emergency_vehicle (e12, e13), ru.official_vehicle of kind incident_management (e14), tow (e15) or coroner (e16), or ru.transit_bus (e17) — and s is paved, lies on (st.on_way) a st.highway region the subject occupies, and is governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold).

narrowings.why: "a person shall not drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle in motion is driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
An emergency is read through the conduct that shows it: hazard lamps flashing, or an emergency vehicle showing a lit warning lamp.

"marked" lanes are read from the mapped lane regions; the portions outside them are read as shoulders, medians and dividers, and any footprint position on the controlled-access highway that overlaps no lane.
"lawfully placed" signage is read from the presence of a shoulder_use_permitted sign governing the shoulder.

A permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle is read through the emergency class the vehicle carries (ru.emergency_vehicle), the jurisdiction's designation shown by its livery and equipment.
A tow car's exclusive use in the business of towing is read through the tow livery and equipment that identify ru.official_vehicle of kind tow.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject car, moving at 25 m/s on a controlled-access highway, drives along the paved shoulder to pass a queue; no hazard lamps, no shoulder-use sign.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves at 30 m/s in a mainline lane of the controlled-access highway; its footprint overlaps only that lane.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives on the shoulder of a surface street; it never overlaps a controlled-access region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car is on the paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway; the source does not supply kin.speed, so whether it is driven there is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A transit bus (ru.transit_bus) with no hazard or warning lamps moves on a paved shoulder of the controlled-access highway governed by a shoulder_use_permitted sign whose conditions admit transit buses.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject car with hazard lamps flashing moves slowly along the shoulder of the controlled-access highway.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives across the median of the controlled-access highway.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: A private car moves on a shoulder governed by a shoulder_use_permitted sign whose conditions admit only transit buses.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: A tow truck (ru.official_vehicle of kind tow) with no hazard or warning lamps moves on a paved shoulder of the controlled-access highway governed by a shoulder_use_permitted sign with no restriction in its legend.

scenarios.name: branch_6
scenarios.narrative: An ambulance (ru.emergency_vehicle) with no warning lamp lit and no hazard lamps moves on a paved shoulder of the controlled-access highway governed by a shoulder_use_permitted sign with no restriction in its legend.

scenarios.name: branch_7
scenarios.narrative: The same ambulance, no warning lamp lit and no hazard lamps, moves on the paved shoulder of the controlled-access highway where no shoulder-use sign governs the shoulder.

scenarios.name: branch_8
scenarios.narrative: A transit bus with no hazard or warning lamps moves on an unpaved shoulder of the controlled-access highway governed by a shoulder_use_permitted sign whose conditions admit transit buses.
